key_insight: Zero-shot large language models improved the positive predictive value–yield trade-off for identifying interstitial lung disease (ILD) compared with published claims-based algorithms.
clinical_relevance: More accurate ILD identification could strengthen cancer-drug safety studies by reducing outcome misclassification and preserving toxicity signals.
method: Evaluated 12 open-access LLMs using claims, clinical notes, or both, without task-specific training.
Compared performance with 20 published claims-based algorithms using positive predictive value (PPV) and yield.
Projected effects of outcome misclassification on drug-safety odds ratios and study sample sizes.
evidence_signal: Among 309 oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes and pulmonologist-adjudicated outcomes, claims-only Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% PPV at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% PPV at 4.9% yield for the highest-PPV algorithm.
watch_item: Validation beyond this single-health-system, diagnosis-code-selected cohort is needed; projected drug-safety benefits were simulated, not demonstrated in a prospective study.
paper_title: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
